---
description: "How NCodeGroup libraries register, resolve, scope and compose services with Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection and NCode.Registration. Covers lifetimes and captive dependencies, TryAdd versus TryAddEnumerable, strategy collections, decorators, marker builders, package boundaries and host-owned infrastructure."
applyTo: "**/*.cs, **/*.csproj"
---

# Dependency injection

<!-- Generated by `npm run train` from the sources each rule cites. To change a rule for good, change its source or say so in training/feedback.md; the next training run regenerates this file. -->

- **Do not cache resolved handler instances in a singleton, and do not resolve scoped services from the root provider. Resolve them from the current scope at the point of use, on every dispatch. Caching reflection results such as closed generic service types is fine.** A cached instance or a root-provider resolution turns scoped dependencies such as a DbContext or tenant persistence into captive dependencies. They then get shared across requests and tenants. *Check:* Look for singletons that keep resolved handlers or services in fields, dictionaries or lazies, and for `GetService`/`GetServices` calls on a root `IServiceProvider` that return scoped services. <sub>Identity ADR-0047; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Run each unit of background work (a job, work item, retry attempt or tenant pass) in its own scope. Create it with `await using var scope = scopeFactory.CreateAsyncScope()` and resolve every handler for that unit from that scope. Dispose any context you create before you dispose the scope. In a loop over tenants, use one scope per tenant, and catch and log each tenant's failure so the remaining tenants still run.** Background work has no request scope. Sharing one scope across items or tenants, or resolving from the root, leaks scoped state across work items and tenants. One tenant's exception must not abort the work for the others. *Check:* Look for hosted or background services that inject scoped services directly, use one `IServiceScope` for many items or tenants, call the synchronous `CreateScope()` in async code, skip `await using`, dispose the scope before its context, or let an exception from one tenant escape the loop. <sub>Identity ADR-0090; Identity ADR-0223; Identity ADR-0232; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Never store a captured `HttpContext`, a request-scoped `IServiceProvider` or a `ClaimsPrincipal` in a field or property. Use a live view over `IHttpContextAccessor`, or pass the value as a method parameter.** Captured request state goes stale and causes use-after-request bugs. *Check:* Look for fields or properties of type `HttpContext`, `IServiceProvider` (scoped) or `ClaimsPrincipal` on long-lived or reusable types. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Give `IValidateOptions<T>` implementations no constructor dependencies, and register each one next to the services that read its options. Never resolve services that have their own dependency graphs inside options validation or in any catalog or data source a validator reads. Feed validators from dependency-free descriptors registered beside each strategy.** If constructing a validator's dependencies reads `IOptions<T>.Value`, host composition deadlocks. The container cannot detect the cycle because its last edge is a runtime `GetServices` call. *Check:* Look for validator constructors that take parameters, especially `IOptions`/`IOptionsMonitor`, `IServiceProvider` or `IEnumerable<IHandler>`, and for catalogs used by validators that resolve handlers just to read a property such as a name. <sub>Identity ADR-0207; Identity ADR-0221; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Do not rely on generic variance when resolving from Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection. To reach handlers registered for base types, explicitly close the open generic over each type in the hierarchy.** MS.DI ignores variance, so `GetServices<IHandler<Derived>>()` does not return handlers registered as `IHandler<Base>`. *Check:* Look for code that expects resolving a derived closed generic to also return handlers registered for a base or interface type argument. <sub>Identity ADR-0047</sub>
- **Make a DI decorator extension work in either registration order. Replace the last non-keyed descriptor in place with one of the same lifetime that wraps its instance, its factory or its implementation type. If there is no descriptor yet, register the decorator around the default implementation so the framework's later `TryAdd` leaves it alone. Never wrap an inner service that is already an instance of the same decorator.** The host may register its implementation before or after the library call. Wrapping twice applies the decorator's transformation, such as normalization, twice. *Check:* Look for decorators that only append a descriptor, change the lifetime, handle only implementation-type descriptors, break when a `TryAdd` runs after them, or wrap without an `inner is TDecorator` guard. <sub>Identity ADR-0243</sub>
- **Register a library's default implementation of any replaceable service, seam, extension point or shared helper service with `TryAdd*` (for example `TryAddSingleton<IFoo, DefaultFoo>()`), so a host or feature package that registers its own implementation keeps it.** With `Add*`, a deployment can no longer replace the default, or it ends up with duplicate registrations where callers get inconsistent implementations. *Check:* Look for `AddSingleton`/`AddScoped`/`AddTransient` of default implementations of extensibility interfaces in library registration code. <sub>Identity ADR-0015; Identity ADR-0016; Identity ADR-0086; Identity ADR-0091; Identity ADR-0093; Identity ADR-0095; Identity ADR-0106; Identity ADR-0111; Identity ADR-0181; Identity ADR-0204; Identity ADR-0205; Identity ADR-0230; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Register every implementation of a strategy collection (handlers, rules, validators, descriptors, algorithm variants, or any multi-subscriber service consumed as `IEnumerable<T>`) with `TryAddEnumerable`, so implementations coexist and packages add more with a single registration.** `AddSingleton`/`TryAddSingleton` replaces or suppresses other subscribers. Plain `Add` allows duplicates. *Check:* Look for interfaces consumed as `IEnumerable<T>` or as multi-handler sets whose implementations are registered with `Add*` or `TryAdd*` instead of `TryAddEnumerable`. <sub>Identity ADR-0001; Identity ADR-0047; Identity ADR-0067; Identity ADR-0079; Identity ADR-0098; Identity ADR-0106; Identity ADR-0117; Identity ADR-0205; Identity ADR-0206; Identity ADR-0226; Identity ADR-0236; Identity ADR-0270</sub>
- **Make each strategy registered with `TryAddEnumerable` its own class. Never register several instances or factories of one implementation type, and never bundle several strategies into one class.** `TryAddEnumerable` deduplicates by implementation type, so only the first instance of a repeated class survives and the others are silently dropped. *Check:* Look for several `TryAddEnumerable` registrations whose instances or factories share one implementation type, or for one class that implements several strategies. <sub>Identity ADR-0206; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Do not pick behavior with a `switch` or if-chain over an open vocabulary (protocol values, algorithm or method names, encodings, response modes). Model each member as a strategy registered with `TryAddEnumerable` and look it up by name, through a catalog or `ICollectionDataSource<T>`. When the catalog is composed, it must reject duplicate names, empty names and references to entries that are not registered.** Hard-coded dispatch closes a vocabulary that nothing proves is closed, so a member another package adds has no behavior. Validating at composition time fails at startup, not later when data is read. *Check:* Look for switches over string constants or growable enums that select an implementation, catalogs that silently accept duplicate names, and validation that only happens at lookup time. <sub>Identity ADR-0079; Identity ADR-0150; Identity ADR-0190; Identity ADR-0201; Identity ADR-0270; Identity ADR-0289</sub>
- **Make dependencies that enforce security or isolation, such as a data context's tenant accessor, required, non-nullable constructor parameters. Represent states like 'no tenant' as values on the dependency, not as a missing dependency. Tests that build the type directly must pass an explicit no-op or no-tenant value.** A required dependency fails fast when it is not registered. An optional one silently runs without isolation, for example leaking data across tenants. *Check:* Look for nullable or optional constructor parameters for tenant or security accessors, `?? default` fallbacks around a missing accessor, or tests passing `null`. <sub>Identity ADR-0018</sub>
- **Make the default for a seam a deployment must supply fail safely: it reports unsupported, undecided or not found, reusing an existing disposition where one fits, and never resolves or approves. When the caller must tell 'not configured' apart from 'rejected', inject the seam as a nullable dependency that is absent by default instead of registering a no-op default.** A default that succeeds is insecure. A no-op that returns null makes 'feature not configured' look the same as 'operation rejected'. *Check:* Look for seam defaults that resolve users, approve requests or pretend to succeed, newly invented dispositions where an existing one fits, and null-returning defaults where the caller has to tell absence apart from rejection. <sub>Identity ADR-0051; Identity ADR-0085; Identity ADR-0086</sub>
- **When adding a member to an existing service would create a constructor-dependency cycle, put that member on a separate interface.** A cycle breaks resolution of everything in that constructor graph. *Check:* Look for new members or dependencies on a service that, directly or transitively, depend back on that service. <sub>Identity ADR-0229</sub>
- **Implement a startup check that depends on state a hosted service loads as an `IHostedService` inserted after that service, not as `ValidateOnStart`, an `IStartupFilter` or an options validator. Check requirements on request-scoped services at the point of use, and throw only on the code paths that actually need them.** Startup validators run before any hosted service starts, and request-dependent services cannot be built at startup. Operations that don't need the service should not fail. *Check:* Look for startup validators that use data a hosted service warms up, gate services added with `AddHostedService` where their order matters, and startup code that resolves request-dependent services from the root provider. <sub>Identity ADR-0243; Identity ADR-0247</sub>
- **Library registration must not make host-wide infrastructure decisions. Do not register `IDistributedCache` (`AddDistributedMemoryCache`, `AddStackExchangeRedisCache`), do not call Data Protection `PersistKeysTo*`, and do not call Kestrel's `ConfigureHttpsDefaults`/`ConfigureKestrel` or change client-certificate modes.** The host's composition root owns these choices. `ConfigureHttpsDefaults` keeps only its last action, so a library call silently overrides the host or gets overridden by it. *Check:* Look for these calls inside library `Add*` or registration extensions rather than host startup code. <sub>Identity ADR-0073; Identity ADR-0164; Identity ADR-0202; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Have a package's registration add the framework services its components need (for example `AddDataProtection()` when `IKeyManager` is used, routing, `IHttpClientFactory`, `AddAuthentication()`) as overridable defaults, and register `TimeProvider.System` with `TryAdd`.** Required dependencies must always resolve without the host adding plumbing, and the host stays free to substitute its own implementations such as a `TimeProvider`. *Check:* Look for components that resolve framework services their package never registers, hosts adding plumbing on a package's behalf, and `TimeProvider` registered with `Add` instead of `TryAdd`. *Note:* This rule covers registering a framework service. Choosing where it persists or how it is configured host-wide still belongs to the host (see the host-infrastructure rule). <sub>Identity ADR-0247; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Put a registration that replaces, hooks, decorates or consumes another library's services on that library's `IServiceBuilder<TMarker>` from `NCode.Registration`, not on a bare `IServiceCollection`. Pass any further prerequisite as a required `IServiceBuilder<TPrereq>` parameter.** The marker receiver proves at compile time that the prerequisite is registered. A bare collection lets a bolt-on be added without its library, which surfaces much later as a missing handler, a null, or an 'unsupported' response. *Check:* Look for `AddX(this IServiceCollection ...)` or `extension(IServiceCollection ...)` methods that depend on another NCode library. Litmus test: would it work if it were the only thing registered? Also flag runtime `IsRegistered`/`VerifyIsRegistered` checks, marker struct or ticket parameters used as proof, and composite `IServiceBuilder<T1,T2>`/`And(...)` combinators. *Note:* ADR-0117 describes opt-in packages enabled with a single `IServiceCollection` extension. The more recent ADR-0069 overrides this whenever the package depends on another library. <sub>Identity ADR-0060; Identity ADR-0069; Identity ADR-0070; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Have every registration that others depend on return its `IServiceBuilder<TMarker>`, including every implementation of a dependency-inverted seam and any custom store, never `void` or `IServiceCollection`.** Dependents need the returned builder as compile-time proof that the prerequisite is present, and that proof cannot be forged. *Check:* Look for prerequisite or seam-implementation registrations that return `void` or `IServiceCollection`, or that never create the seam's marker builder. <sub>Identity ADR-0060; Identity ADR-0069</sub>
- **Use a bare `IServiceCollection` receiver only for chain roots that create a marker and have no prerequisite, for standalone single-service utilities, and for cross-cutting infrastructure that creates no marker. Give helpers shared by several libraries' builders the non-generic `IServiceBuilder` receiver.** Anything else on a bare collection gives up the compile-time guarantee. Pinning a shared helper to one marker breaks its other callers. *Check:* For each bare-collection registration in the diff, confirm it is one of the allowed kinds. Development helpers that `Replace` services or add handlers for a library must take that library's builder. Look for shared helpers typed to a specific `IServiceBuilder<T>` or to `IServiceCollection`. <sub>Identity ADR-0069; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **A builder or context type that lets callers register services, such as an endpoint-group builder, should inherit `IServiceBuilder` and not expose an `IServiceCollection Services` property.** A bare collection cannot reach builder-level helpers, and it creates a second, parallel registration vocabulary. *Check:* Look for new builder or context interfaces that expose `IServiceCollection` for registration. <sub>Identity ADR-0043</sub>
- **Define each registration marker as an empty `readonly struct` that implements `IRegistrationMarker<TMarker>`.** The marker's type identity is the whole signal. Members only add per-marker data that has to be kept in sync. *Check:* Look for marker types that are classes, are not readonly, or declare members. <sub>Identity ADR-0069</sub>
- **Register each package's services in a single class named `DefaultRegistration` using `extension(IServiceBuilder<TMarker>)` and `TryAdd*`. Name the package-root method `AddXLibrary()`; it returns `builder.NewBuilder<XLibrary>()`. Each purpose folder gets its own `AddYServices()` that returns the receiver builder. Bolt-ons return the receiver and create no new library marker.** Consistent nesting shows at each call site where a new marker scope begins, and it avoids catch-all registration grab-bags. *Check:* Look for registrations outside `DefaultRegistration`, unrelated folders registered in one catch-all method, new purpose folders without their own `Add…Services`, and root or folder methods whose naming or return value doesn't match. <sub>Identity ADR-0016; Identity ADR-0069; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Compose hosts by chaining registrations off the builders returned by the composition root and the library registrations, not by calling capability methods on `services`.** Chaining enforces prerequisites at compile time and shows the dependency order. *Check:* Look in host startup code for capability or bolt-on registrations called directly on `IServiceCollection`. <sub>Identity ADR-0069</sub>
- **Implementation packages reference only `*.Abstractions` packages. Only the composition root references implementation packages and calls their registrations. Collaborate across packages by constructor-injecting the abstraction (`IFoo`), never the other package's concrete type (`DefaultFoo`), and register only your own package's concrete types.** This keeps every implementation replaceable, gives each shared behavior exactly one binding, and keeps the reference graph a flat fan-out from the root. *Check:* Look for `ProjectReference`/`PackageReference` from an implementation project to a non-Abstractions package outside the composition root, `new DefaultFoo(...)` or `DefaultFoo` constructor parameters from other packages, and registrations of another package's concrete types. <sub>Identity ADR-0016; Identity ADR-0290; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Make a reusable capability that needs a pluggable backend depend only on a seam interface in its `.Abstractions` package. Put the concrete backend implementation in the package that already owns that backend, registered by that package's own opt-in method. The capability's base registration wires no concrete backend.** The surface stays backend-agnostic, so alternatives such as LDAP, an external IdP or passwordless plug in without forking it. *Check:* Look for capability handlers that inject concrete stores, persistence, JOSE or crypto types, and for base `Add…()` registrations that register a concrete backend. *Note:* A safe, failing default (see the seam-defaults rule) is still allowed. What this rule forbids is a concrete backend in the base registration. <sub>Identity ADR-0070</sub>
- **Pick the DI shape deliberately. Use a service (`TryAddSingleton<IFoo, DefaultFoo>`) when the caller wants one deterministic answer. Use a `TryAddEnumerable` strategy collection when the caller iterates over or selects among implementations. Use an NCode.Mediator command fan-out only when you need a real pipeline seam: priority ordering, pre/post processors, unified exception handling, or open-ended contributors the sender must not know about, such as reactions to a state change. Model orchestration and side-effecting transports, such as delivery or notification, as replaceable services called from handlers.** Routing a fixed capability through the mediator hides it from navigation and adds overhead for nothing. Bespoke provider or seeder interfaces, or side effects hard-coded inline, fragment extensibility. *Check:* Look for mediator commands with one fixed handler whose result the sender consumes, commands that only wrap a transport, orchestration modelled as a command, new ad-hoc `IXxxProvider`/`IXxxSeeder` collections where a fan-out fits, and services that perform several reactive side effects inline. *Note:* ADR-0001 prefers a strategy collection when no pipeline semantics are needed. ADR-0045/0098 prefer the mediator fan-out when contributors need priority ordering. Choose based on whether pipeline semantics are actually required. <sub>Identity ADR-0001; Identity ADR-0045; Identity ADR-0086; Identity ADR-0098; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Order mediator handlers that depend on each other's effects with explicit `ISupportMediatorPriority` values (High for observers and repairers, Low for consumers), never with registration order. A validation handler chained after others returns at once when an error is already set.** Registration order is fragile and implicit. Overwriting an existing error hides the original failure. *Check:* Look for handlers that rely on another handler's effect without a priority, comments that depend on registration order, and chained validators that set an error without checking for an existing one. <sub>Identity ADR-0226; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Map each endpoint exactly once. Register an endpoint family, its provider and its dependent services (including message factories) through one extension on the endpoint-group builder, and never also through the flat root endpoint collection or a separate chain.** Double registration maps the endpoint twice, and the copy outside the group misses the group's filters and conventions. *Check:* Look for an endpoint or provider registered in more than one place, or its dependencies registered apart from its group. <sub>Identity ADR-0009; Identity ADR-0043</sub>
- **A capability that adds endpoints or services to a composition point it does not own registers them as keyed services under the owner's published key constant, without editing the owner.** The owner maps only its own families, and capabilities plug in without the owner knowing about them. *Check:* Look for edits to an owning group that reference a capability's handler directly, or hard-coded group-name strings used in place of the published key. <sub>Identity ADR-0061</sub>
- **Ship optional features, including dev- or conformance-grade login and consent modules, as explicit opt-in registrations that default registration never calls. The capability is present exactly when its registration was called. Do not add per-request 'is it registered' checks such as returning 501, or marker services the library uses only to detect itself.** Always-on optional features add dependencies and attack surface. Self-detection guards are dead weight, because the opt-in call already answers the question. *Check:* Look for optional or dev modules wired from default `Add*` methods or unconditionally in production setup, handlers that return 501 when an optional service is missing, and capability-marker services. <sub>Identity ADR-0061; Identity ADR-0062; Identity ADR-0065; Identity ADR-0117</sub>
- **Make optional pieces degrade gracefully. When an optional alternate formatter is not registered, fall back to the default representation. A selectable provider that is registered but not selected skips its startup validation and creates no client or credential until its first real operation.** Hosts without the optional package must still work. Registering several providers must not require configuring every one of them or opening connections to them. *Check:* Look for code that throws when an optional formatter is absent, provider validators that ignore the selector, and constructors or factories that eagerly create SDK clients or credentials. <sub>Identity ADR-0114; Identity ADR-0260</sub>
- **Constructor-inject every collaborator. Do not `new` services and do not use a service locator, except in a singleton that resolves scoped or generically selected services at the point of use. Resolve pluggable mechanisms such as chain validators and revocation checkers from DI rather than constructing them in handlers.** Injection keeps code testable and lets deployments replace mechanisms without editing handlers or extending policy enums. *Check:* Look for `new` of service collaborators inside methods, `GetService` calls where injection was possible, and new policy enum values added only to support a different mechanism. <sub>Identity ADR-0173; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Expose a policy that replaceable public services reuse as a public interface in the abstractions package, keep its default implementation internal, and register that default with `TryAdd`.** A public concrete class fixes the policy's dependencies into the public API. An internal-only policy forces every replacement to reimplement it. *Check:* Look for replaceable policies exposed as public concrete classes, or replacements that would need internal types to behave like the default. <sub>Identity ADR-0181</sub>
- **Declare delegates the host can replace on a shared environment abstraction in `*.Abstractions`, wired from the core options delegate. Consumers call the hook through that abstraction, not by injecting the core `IOptions<TOptions>`.** Packages that depend only on abstractions cannot inject the core options, so they end up writing their own versions of the hook, and the versions drift apart. *Check:* Look for non-core packages that inject a core `IOptions<...Options>` just to call a behavioral delegate, and new delegates reachable only through the options type. <sub>Identity ADR-0053</sub>
- **Register stateless capabilities as singletons behind interfaces instead of static utility classes, keep no static mutable or ambient state, and host long-running loops with `AddHostedService<T>` over a `BackgroundService`, with registration kept outside the worker type.** A singleton costs about the same as a static and stays mockable, while static state hurts testability. *Check:* Look for new static classes with logic that has dependencies, mutable static fields, and worker types that register themselves or resolve their own services. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Make an endpoint depend on as few services as possible, ideally only client authentication, and reach the remaining steps through the mediator.** A thin endpoint holds no protocol logic, and its steps stay replaceable. *Check:* Look for endpoint providers whose constructors inject stores, issuers or other protocol services. <sub>Identity ADR-0086</sub>
- **Expose a lazily built service to handlers and hosted services through a singleton registry or accessor that has no dependencies and waits until the service exists. Do not have them depend on the services that build it.** Consumers then reach the service without pulling in its construction graph or creating cycles. *Check:* Look for hosted services or handlers that inject a provider or factory only to get an already-built instance, or that build it themselves. <sub>Identity ADR-0219</sub>
- **In tests that compose services needing an unrelated dependency, register a strict mock that is never called (`new Mock<T>(MockBehavior.Strict).Object`). Do not disable DI validation or wire up a real backend.** DI validation stays on while the configuration under test stays isolated. *Check:* Look for tests that set `ValidateOnBuild` or `ValidateScopes` to false, or that wire a real database, only to satisfy composition. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp-testing.instructions.md</sub>
